issues.description: Method Milkable.messageOnMilk(): the problem statement (UML and textual instructions) declares messageOnMilk() to return a boolean (e.g. "return true if milking was successful, false otherwise"), but the provided solution code declares the interface method as returning a String and concrete classes (Seal, Goat) implement it as returning a String (e.g. "Seal <name> is milked"). This inconsistency leaves students unsure whether to implement messageOnMilk() with signature boolean messageOnMilk() (as per UML/text) or String messageOnMilk() (as per template/solution), and will cause compilation/test mismatches depending on which is expected by the tests.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the return type for Milkable.messageOnMilk() consistent across all artifacts. Recommended (least disruptive): update the problem statement UML and the textual description to specify that messageOnMilk() returns a String and include an example (e.g. ""Goat <name> is milked""), so it matches the template usage and the solution implementation. Alternatively, if boolean semantics are intended, change the template and solution to declare Milkable.messageOnMilk() as boolean and update all implementations and example outputs/tests accordingly.
